user.title: Add BattMind
user.description:
BattMind plans when the home battery should charge from the grid, discharge or sell, based on prices, consumption and solar forecast. The plan is published as sensors you use in your own automations.

**Entity prefix** is used in every entity id, e.g. `sensor.PREFIX_powerwall_action`. Use a different prefix for each instance (and another prefix than the PyScript version if both run). It cannot be changed later.

data_description.language: Language used for entity names, the overview, charging history, charging rule and notifications.
data_description.dashboard_icon: Icon of the dashboard in the sidebar, e.g. mdi:home-battery. Leave empty for the default icon.

import_legacy.title: Import from the PyScript version

price_provider.title: Electricity prices
price_provider.description: Choose where the hourly prices come from. With both, the first one with a price for an hour is used and the other fills the gaps.

battery_entities.title: Home battery - sensors
battery_entities.description: The sensors BattMind reads from your home battery / inverter.

data_description.powerwall_battery_level_entity_id: Sensor with the home battery state of charge in percent (0-100 %).
data_description.powerwall_watt_flow_entity_id: Sensor with the power into/out of the battery (W or kW). Expected: positive when discharging, negative when charging. Tip: block battery discharging while the EV is charging.
data_description.battery_temperature_entity_id: Optional temperature sensor. When configured, BattMind stops the battery outside the safe range or while the sensor is unavailable.

battery_specs.title: Home battery - specifications
battery_specs.description: Used to convert between % and kWh, to limit the plan and to calculate what the energy in the battery costs.

data_description.powerwall_battery_size: Usable capacity of the home battery.
data_description.powerwall_battery_level_min: BattMind never plans below this level (the reserve you keep in the battery).
data_description.powerwall_battery_level_max: BattMind never plans charging above this level.
data_description.battery_temperature_min: Stop charging and discharging below this temperature. Use the battery manufacturer's limit.
data_description.battery_temperature_max: Stop charging and discharging above this temperature. Use the battery manufacturer's limit.
data_description.powerwall_charging_power_limit: Highest power the battery charges with. Used to calculate how many kWh can be charged per hour.
data_description.powerwall_discharging_power: Highest power the battery discharges with. Limits how much can be sold per hour.
data_description.powerwall_charge_discharge_loss: Round-trip loss as a fraction: 0.1 = 10 % loss. Added to the price of the energy in the battery.
data_description.use_charge_discharge_loss_from_history: Calculate the loss from the charging history instead (used after 6 full charge cycles of history).
data_description.battery_charging_efficiency_curve: Map AC charging power in W to efficiency in percent, for example 1000 W = 88 %, 3000 W = 94 %, 5000 W = 96 %. BattMind interpolates between points. Leave empty to let BattMind measure the curve itself (the round-trip loss is used until there are enough measurements).
data_description.battery_discharging_efficiency_curve: Map AC discharging power in W to efficiency in percent, for example 500 W = 82 %, 2000 W = 93 %, 5000 W = 96 %. BattMind interpolates between points. Leave empty to let BattMind measure the curve itself (the round-trip loss is used until there are enough measurements).
data_description.powerwall_wear_cost_per_kwh: Cost of wear per kWh taken from the battery (battery price / expected lifetime in kWh). Discharging must earn more than this.

battery_actions.title: Home battery - controllable modes
battery_actions.description: BattMind plans with these battery modes (the sensor Powerwall action). If your inverter can't run a mode, select it here. BattMind then never plans it, and the rules that need it are switched off. Normal operation (discharge_allowed) and the temperature safety stop are always used. Leave everything unselected if the battery can run every mode.

data_description.unsupported_actions: Grid charging: the grid charging rules are off (cheapest periods, most expensive periods, required before max level, negative prices, buy to sell). Force discharge: selling from the battery is off (maximise profit, sell excess kWh, before the sun, buy to sell); old energy is only used, not sold. Solar only charging: holding the energy for later is off (profit only, prioritise by energy cost, maximise profit). Block solar charging: optimise solar charging is off. The switches keep their value, but count as off.

consumption.title: House consumption
consumption.description:
BattMind stores the consumption per hour and predicts how much the battery must cover the next days.

Cable Juice Planner chargers found: {cjp_chargers}

data_description.power_consumption_entity_id: Sensor with the house consumption (W/kW) - not the grid import. The history is used to predict the consumption per hour.
data_description.ignore_consumption_from_entity_ids: Power sensors that are subtracted from the house consumption, e.g. EV chargers that should not be covered by the battery.
data_description.ignore_cjp_chargers: Subtracts the charging power of the chargers of your Cable Juice Planner cars from the house consumption, also for cars added later. A charger that is also in the list above is only subtracted once. Turn off if your house consumption sensor does not include the chargers.

detection_review.title: Check the battery and consumption settings
detection_review.description:
Suggested from the recorded history of the battery and house consumption sensors, as far back as needed. Check the numbers – you can change everything.

In the brackets: h = hours of unbroken data, n = battery switch-overs compared, and how far back it was found.

✅ = on, ⬜ = off, ❔ = could not be determined (also when charging and discharging do not point to the same kind of sensor): the current value is kept. Nothing is looked up again while the sensors are unchanged; tick *Detect again* to do it.

**Battery power sign** {invert_mark} ({invert_window})
The battery level went from {soc_start} to {soc_end} % while the average battery power was {power_avg} W. A rising level with positive power means positive = charging: turn *Invert power flow* on.

**Consumption includes charging** {charging_mark} ({charging_window})
Around the moments the battery started or stopped charging, the house consumption was {c_charging} W while it charged {p_charging} W, against {c_idle_charging} W just before or after, when it was idle. A step of about the charging power means it includes it; no step means it does not.

**Consumption includes discharging** {discharging_mark} ({discharging_window})
Around the moments the battery started or stopped discharging, the house consumption was {c_discharging} W while it discharged {p_discharging} W, against {c_idle_discharging} W just before or after, when it was idle. A fall of about the discharge power means it does not include it; no fall means it does (if the house uses at least as much as the battery gives).

data_description.invert_powerwall_watt_flow_entity_id: Enable if your sensor is positive when charging and negative when discharging.
data_description.power_consumption_entity_id_include_powe: Enable if the consumption sensor includes the power used to charge the battery.
Enable if the consumption sensor already includes the consumption covered by the battery.
data_description.redetect: Looks at the recorder again for the three sensors and puts what it finds in the settings above. Nothing is saved until you continue without it.

prices_energidataservice.title: Energi Data Service
prices_energidataservice.description: Sensors from the [Energi Data Service]({eds_url}) integration. Enable Carnot (AI price forecast) in Energi Data Service to plan more than the published prices.

data_description.energidataservice_buy_entity_id: The Energi Data Service sensor with the total price incl. tariffs (attributes raw_today/raw_tomorrow/forecast).
data_description.energidataservice_sell_entity_id: A separate Energi Data Service sensor for the sell price. Empty = the buy price minus tariffs is used.

prices_stromligning.title: Strømligning

data_description.stromligning_buy_current_price: Strømligning current price incl. VAT (e.g. sensor.stromligning_current_price_vat).
data_description.stromligning_buy_tomorrow_available: Strømligning ’tomorrow available’ entity for the buy price.
data_description.stromligning_buy_forecasts: Strømligning forecast sensor - used for the hours where no real price is published yet.
data_description.stromligning_sell_current_price: Strømligning current price excl. VAT for selling (e.g. the 15 min ex_vat sensor). Enables the tariff page.
data_description.stromligning_sell_tomorrow_available: Strømligning ’tomorrow available’ entity for the sell price.
data_description.stromligning_sell_forecasts: Strømligning forecast sensor for the sell price.

prices_stromligning_tariffs.title: Strømligning - tariffs for selling

data_description.stromligning_sell_distribution: The grid company's distribution (transport) tariff per period. Subtracted when the sell price is calculated (days without a tariff use the same time of the latest known day).
data_description.stromligning_sell_electricity_tax: Electricity tax sensor. Subtracted when the sell price is calculated.
data_description.stromligning_sell_nettariff: Net tariff sensor. Subtracted when the sell price is calculated.
data_description.stromligning_sell_systemtariff: System tariff sensor. Subtracted from the sell price, and again as a selling cost.
data_description.stromligning_sell_surcharge: The supplier surcharge on the spot price. Subtracted when the sell price is calculated.

price_fees.title: Refund and fees
price_fees.description: Amounts per kWh that change what charging and selling is worth.

data_description.refund: Refund per kWh from state/grid company/supplier, subtracted from the buy price in the price history. 0 if none.
data_description.sell_fee: Fee per kWh when selling to the grid. Included in the calculated sell price.

solar.title: Solar panels

data.production_price: Fixed sell price for solar surplus

data_description.production_entity_id: Sensor with the current solar production (W/kW). Leave empty if you have no solar panels.
data_description.inverter_discharging_power_limit: Max AC power of the inverter. Limits how much solar + battery power is available at the same time.
data_description.production_price: Price per kWh (in the currency of Home Assistant) used to value solar surplus that is sold, e.g. a fixed price from your electricity company. Set to -1 to use the hourly sell price.
data_description.forecast_entity_id: Solcast PV Forecast sensor, e.g. sensor.solcast_pv_forecast_forecast_today. The days ahead are found automatically.

weather.title: Weather forecast
weather.description: Used together with the stored solar history to predict the solar surplus. Any weather integration supporting `weather.get_forecasts` works (Met.no, AccuWeather, OpenWeather, ...).

data_description.hourly_service_entity_id: Weather entity supporting hourly forecasts. Cloud cover, UV and temperature are used to estimate the solar surplus.
data_description.daily_service_entity_id: Weather entity supporting daily forecasts. Used for the hours the hourly forecast does not cover.

advanced.title: Planning
advanced.description: The planner, rules and thresholds are controlled from the BattMind entities (switches and numbers) - these are the technical settings.

data_description.days_to_predict: Number of days (incl. today) the charging plan, the consumption prediction and the solar prediction cover. More days give better decisions about storing energy, but cost more CPU and depend on price forecasts.
data_description.cron_interval: Minutes between each check of the plan. The plan is only recalculated when prices, battery level or settings changed.
data_description.dashboard: Adds a ready-made BattMind dashboard to the sidebar with the plan, prices, history and all settings for this instance. Needs the HACS cards apexcharts-card, mushroom, config-template-card, timer-bar-card and card-mod (optional). A notification lists missing cards.
data_description.enable_diagnostic_file_log: Write a detailed log to battmind_{prefix}.log in the config folder (2 MB per file, 3 rotations). For troubleshooting.

database.title: Data storage
database.description: How much history BattMind keeps. More history gives more stable predictions but adapts slower to changes.

data_description.power_values_db_data_to_save: Number of days of consumption per hour kept for the consumption prediction.
data_description.solar_available_db_data_to_save: Number of measurements of solar surplus kept per hour and weather score.
data_description.kwh_avg_prices_db_data_to_save: Number of days of prices kept. Used as fallback prices when the price integration is offline.
data_description.charging_history_db_data_to_save: Number of months of charging history kept (shown in the history and used for the battery cost).

restore_backup.title: Restore from a backup
restore_backup.description:
BattMind backups found in **battmind_backups** (written by Export data and when a BattMind device is deleted).

Choose one to restore it as **{prefix}**: its configuration is used as defaults on the next pages, and the databases and settings are restored on first start.

error.detection_recorder: The suggestions could not be made: the recorder is not running, so there is no history. The current values are kept.
error.detection_timeout: Reading the history took too long. The current values are kept; tick *Detect again* to try again.
error.detection_error: The history could not be read. The current values are kept; tick *Detect again* to try again.
error.detection_data: The sensors have no usable history (or it is too short). The current values are kept.
error.detection_unit: A power sensor has an unknown unit (not W, kW …), so the history can't be compared. The current values are kept.
error.invalid_prefix: Use 1-50 lowercase letters, digits or underscores, starting with a letter.
error.prefix_in_use: This prefix is already used by another BattMind entry.
error.prefix_entities_exist: Entities with this prefix already exist (e.g. from the PyScript version). Choose another prefix to run both at the same time.
error.min_above_max: The minimum level must be lower than the maximum level.
error.invalid_icon: Use an icon name like mdi:home-battery.
error.invalid_efficiency_curve: Use an object mapping power above 0 W to an efficiency above 0 and at most 100 percent.
error.no_price_provider: Choose at least one price provider.
error.production_required: A solar forecast requires a solar production sensor.

init.title: BattMind
init.description: Choose what to change. The integration is reloaded when you save.

storm.title: Storm warning
storm.description: Keep the battery charged for a storm warning. Choose MeteoAlarm's binary sensor; leave it empty to turn the function off. Only warnings of wind, snow/ice or thunderstorms at or above the chosen level count, and only warnings with a start time. The need is the expected house use during the warning with no solar, plus a buffer for a forecast that is off (at least 20 %). Without a backup power supply a full battery does not run the house in a power cut.

data_description.storm_warning_entity_id: MeteoAlarm's binary sensor for your region. Empty = off: the function, its sensor and its number are not made.

backup.title: Backup
backup.description:
Export writes the databases, settings and configuration to a file in **battmind_backups**.

Importing a file replaces the databases and settings of **{prefix}** with the backup (the current data is exported first, as a *_before_import* file) and reloads the integration.

data_description.restore_configuration: Use the entities and options of the backup as well. Leave off when the backup comes from another Home Assistant.

what_if.name: What-if simulator
what_if.description: Replays the BattMind planner on up to one year of hourly history. Current is an estimate assuming the current configuration throughout the period, not the actual historical result. Focus on the difference between current and scenario; it is also an estimate. The latest result is saved; the active plan and settings are not changed.

confirm.title: Update the blueprint {name}
confirm.description:
BattMind comes with a version of the blueprint **{name}** that differs from `{path}`.

Select **Submit** to replace the file with the bundled version and reload the automations that use it. Changes you made to the file yourself are overwritten – copy it to another file name first if you want to keep them.

Ignore this repair to keep your own file.

stromligning_entities.title: Strømligning sensors that BattMind needs are not available ({prefix})

solcast_entities.title: Solcast forecast sensors that BattMind needs are not available ({prefix})

entities_missing.title: Sensors BattMind uses are disabled or missing ({prefix})
entities_missing.description:
BattMind ({prefix}) uses sensors that are disabled in Home Assistant, or that no longer exist because they were deleted or renamed. The plan then works with missing values, and the battery may not follow it.

Disabled (enable them under **Settings → Devices & services → Entities**, with *Show disabled entities*):
{disabled}

Missing (select the sensor again under **Configure** in the BattMind integration, or give it its old name back):
{missing}

To check that the battery still follows the plan, run *Test my automation* on the BattMind dashboard.

This repair disappears by itself when all the sensors are enabled and found again.

entity_units.title: Sensor units BattMind can't read ({prefix})
entity_units.description:
BattMind ({prefix}) reads power sensors in mW, W, kW, MW or GW (a unit with an h, such as Wh or kWh, is read as the unit without it), and the battery level in %. These sensors report another unit, so their values are read at the wrong size and the plan is wrong:
{entities}

Change the unit in the integration that creates the sensor, or select a sensor that reports power or the battery level in these units under **Configure** in the BattMind integration. Then run *Test my automation* on the BattMind dashboard to check that the battery still follows the plan.

This repair disappears by itself when every sensor reports a unit BattMind can read.

blueprint_automation_lost.title: The automation made from the BattMind blueprint is off ({prefix})
blueprint_automation_lost.description:
BattMind ({prefix}) has seen an automation made from its battery blueprint switched on. It is now turned off or deleted, so the battery no longer gets the actions of the plan.

Turned off (a dash means the automation was deleted from automations.yaml):
{automations}

Turn the automation on again under **Settings → Automations & scenes**, or make a new one from the BattMind blueprint and run *Test my automation* on the BattMind dashboard.

This repair disappears by itself when the automation is on again. If you stopped using the blueprint on purpose, ignore this repair.

power_without_unit.title: Power sensors without a unit ({prefix})
power_without_unit.description:
BattMind ({prefix}) reads these power sensors in watts (W), since they have no unit. The number after ≤ is the highest value seen (without sign):
{entities}

Over the last {days} days their values never went above {max}, and some of them are decimal numbers. That looks like kilowatts (kW): read as W, the values are 1000 times too small, and the plan uses far too little power.

Fix it at the source: give the sensor its unit, for example `unit_of_measurement: kW` on a template sensor, or the unit that the integration creating the sensor gives. Then run *Test my automation* on the BattMind dashboard to check that the battery still follows the plan.

If the values really are in W, ignore this repair. It disappears by itself when the sensors have a unit, or when their values show that they are in W.

battery_level_fraction.title: The battery level looks like a share, not a percentage ({prefix})
battery_level_fraction.description:
BattMind ({prefix}) reads the battery level sensor as a percentage (%). The number after ≤ is the highest value seen (without sign):
{entities}

Over the last {days} days every value lay between 0 and 1, so it looks like a share (0.85 = 85 %). Read as a percentage, 0.85 is 0.85 % instead of 85 %.

Fix it at the source: make the sensor report 0 to 100, for example by multiplying by 100 in a template sensor, and select that sensor under **Configure** in the BattMind integration. Then run *Test my automation* on the BattMind dashboard to check that the battery still follows the plan.

If the battery level really stays below 1 %, ignore this repair. It disappears by itself when the sensor reports values above 1.

price_unit_scale.title: Price sensors in a subunit, per MWh or per Wh ({prefix})
price_unit_scale.description:
BattMind ({prefix}) reads prices from these sensors, but they are in a unit BattMind does not convert:
{entities}

The prices are in a subunit of the currency (øre or cent), per MWh or per Wh. BattMind does not convert them, so the prices are in another scale: 100 times too large (subunit), 1000 times too large (per MWh) or 1000 times too small (per Wh). The plan and the savings calculation are wrong.

Fix it at the source: in Energi Data Service turn off **Show prices in cent** and set **Price calculated in** to kWh in the integration's options. Or select a sensor with the currency per kWh (e.g. kr/kWh) under **Configure** in the BattMind integration. Then run *Test my automation* on the BattMind dashboard to check that the battery still follows the plan.

If the prices really are in the currency per kWh, ignore this repair. It disappears by itself when no price sensor is in a subunit, per MWh or per Wh.

consumption_frozen.title: House consumption sensor shows the same value ({prefix})
consumption_frozen.description:
BattMind ({prefix}) uses the house consumption sensor {entity} for the plan. It has shown the same value, {value}, since {since}. When a consumption sensor stops changing, the integration or device that delivers it is usually stuck, so the plan uses an old value for the house consumption.

Check the integration or device that delivers this sensor, and restart it if needed. Then run *Test my automation* on the BattMind dashboard to check that the battery still follows the plan.

This repair disappears by itself when the sensor shows another value. It changes nothing in BattMind or your automations: ignore it if the value really is steady.

plan_not_followed.title: The battery does not follow the plan ({prefix})
plan_not_followed.description:
In the last {days} days BattMind judged {checked} hours in which the battery should do what the action of `sensor.{prefix}_powerwall_action` says. In {mismatches} of them the battery did not do it, and {percent} % matched. This repair is raised at {min_checked} or more judged hours with at least {min_mismatches} mismatches and a match below {max_percent} %.

Latest mismatches (hour, action, charged / discharged kWh):
{latest}

Common causes:
- the automation does not run the step for that action: run *Test my automation* on the BattMind dashboard and read the result for each action
- another app, another automation or the inverter's own schedule also controls the battery
- a wrong sign: charging is measured as discharging, or the other way round (check the battery power sensor)
- an inverter setting, such as its minimum state of charge or maximum power, stops the battery

Hours in which the battery could not follow are not counted: the battery was at a limit, the test ran, data was missing, or the action changed during the hour.

This repair disappears by itself when the battery follows the plan again: fewer than {min_mismatches} hours mismatch, or at least {max_percent} % match. The hours are counted over the last {days} days, so this can take several days.
